archetype.name: Pocket Passer (timing-and-rhythm)
archetype.definition: A 38-year-old rhythm thrower who wins from a clean pocket by getting the ball out on schedule to short and outside targets, takes his deep shots off structure, and adds nothing as a runner.

report.headline: A clean-pocket rebound, but the touchdown pace is outrunning the efficiency.
report.take:
Cousins is doing what he has done for most of his career when protected and surrounded by good targets: distributing on time, staying on schedule, and punishing coverage outside the numbers. His 0.169 EPA per dropback ranks 15th of 42. That sits right in his 2019-2021 band with Minnesota and is a clear recovery from a 2025 that looked like decline (6.4 YPA, -2.8 CPOE, 41st in yards per attempt). At 7.13 YPA and +2.3 CPOE this year, he is a functional, above-average starter again. He is not a star, and the sorting stats say so: 20th in completion rate, 21st in YPA and CPOE.

What drives the season is a clean pocket and a tidy short game. He has been pressured on just 14.1% of dropbacks, second-lowest among charted QBs, and sacked on 3.4%. That lets a 2.98-second time to throw work without punishment. Throws inside 10 yards return 0.306 EPA at 74% completion with no picks, and he is equally productive to both sidelines (about +0.30 EPA left and right). Brock Bowers (0.568 EPA per target) and Tre Tucker (0.354) are carrying the efficiency. Ashton Jeanty's team-high 25 targets are a drag at -0.062, and the 15 throws behind the line have cost 0.447 EPA each. The offense needs the pass to work. The run game is 29th in EPA, and Cousins himself has -2 yards on 12 carries.

The numbers flatter him in one place and hide a flaw in another. Eleven touchdowns lead the league, but nine came in the red zone on 26 attempts with only a 37% success rate there. A 7.6% TD rate on 144 attempts is well above anything in his career and will cool. The flaw is the intermediate middle of the field. Throws of 10-19 yards are at 45% completion and 10.7 points under expected, and all four of his interceptions came there. Between the hashes his CPOE is -12.2. The deep numbers, by contrast, look great (0.776 EPA, three TDs), but that is on 17 attempts.

The direction is good: game EPA climbed each week, and he threw for 365 against KC without being sacked even with starting guard Jackson Powers-Johnson inactive. Expect a steady 230-270-yard passer whose touchdowns drift back toward two a game. His value rises and falls with how clean the pocket stays.

strengths.title: Thriving behind a clean pocket
strengths.body: He has been pressured on only 14.1% of dropbacks and sacked on 3.4%, both near the top of the position. His pressure-to-sack rate (23.8%) is middling and consistent with his career, so the low sack total comes from protection and rhythm, not escapability. It holds up as long as the line stays intact. Week 4 with no sacks and Powers-Johnson out was encouraging.

strengths.title: Efficient short game outside numbers
strengths.body: Inside 10 yards he completes 74.4% for 0.306 EPA with six touchdowns and no picks. Throws to both sidelines sit near +0.30 EPA. This is the career-long Cousins skill set: timing, ball placement and staying on schedule. It is the most sustainable part of the profile.

strengths.title: Bowers and Tucker carry the efficiency
strengths.body: Bowers returns 0.568 EPA per target and Tucker 0.354. They are the reason the passing offense ranks 7th in EPA despite a 29th-ranked run game. This depends on Bowers staying healthy. With Bech on IR and Nailor concussed, the target tree behind them is thin.

concerns.title: Intermediate middle is where turnovers live
concerns.body: On 10-19 yard throws he is completing 45.2%, 10.7 points under expected, and all four interceptions came in that band. Over the middle his CPOE is -12.2. Only 31 attempts, so some of this is noise. Still, his bad-throw rate and 2025's accuracy dip make it worth watching as a real arm or anticipation limitation at 38.

concerns.title: Touchdown rate is running hot
concerns.body: Nine of his 11 TDs came in the red zone, where he is only 13 of 26 with a 37% success rate. A 7.6% TD rate is above any full season in his career. Expect the TD count to regress even if the yardage holds. That matters for fantasy and TD props more than for real efficiency.

concerns.title: Checkdowns to Jeanty leak value
concerns.body: Jeanty is the most-targeted player at -0.062 EPA per target, and throws behind the line return -0.447 EPA. Some of that is the price of a quick, safe game plan with a dead run game. It still caps the offense's ceiling whenever Bowers and Tucker are covered.

trend.note: Game passing EPA has climbed every week (0.4, 6, 9, 9.8). After a two-pick opener against Miami, his bad-throw rate fell from 17.2% to about 10%. Week 4 brought a 52-attempt, 365-yard volume spike in a shootout loss to KC.

nextGame.headline: A top-five pass defense, but missing its No. 1 corner
nextGame.body:
New England's defense profiles as tough on paper for a passer: 5th in pass EPA allowed, 5th-fewest QB yards allowed per game (218) and 7th-fewest QB fantasy points. Two cracks fit Cousins's profile, though. The Patriots are 21st in deep EPA allowed, and their pass rush is ordinary (19th in sack rate, 16th in hit rate), so the clean pockets he has been living in should largely continue. Their run defense is 30th, which in theory gives the Raiders' broken ground game a rare opening to stay balanced.

Availability tilts toward the Raiders' passing game. Christian Gonzalez (95% of snaps) is out, CB Charles Woods is questionable and Channing Canada is out, so the secondary is thin. DT Christian Barmore being out also softens the interior rush. On the Raiders' side, Powers-Johnson's return date lines up with this game but isn't confirmed. Nailor (concussion) is questionable, and Bech remains on IR. Dont'e Thornton's possible return would add a body, but Bowers and Tucker will carry the load again.

keyMatchups.title: Raiders' targets vs. a corner-depleted secondary
keyMatchups.body: Without Gonzalez, and with Woods banged up, New England has to cover Tucker outside and Bowers everywhere with depth pieces. Cousins is at his best throwing to the sidelines. This is the most likely path to beating the Patriots' strong season-long pass numbers.

keyMatchups.title: Shot plays against a leaky deep defense
keyMatchups.body: NE gives up 0.683 EPA on deep throws (21st), and Cousins has 0.776 EPA on his 17 deep attempts. Both samples are small, but they point the same way. One or two connections could swing the game.

keyMatchups.title: Raiders defense vs. a middling offense
keyMatchups.body: Las Vegas's defense is 2nd in EPA and 3rd against the pass, facing a New England offense 22nd in EPA. If the defense controls the game, Cousins won't need another 52-attempt day. That keeps him efficient but limits volume.

nextGame.watch: Whether he keeps forcing 10-19 yard throws between the hashes, where every one of his interceptions has come, or lets the sideline and short game do the work against backup corners.

restOfSeason.body:
The foundation is real and matches his long track record: good short accuracy, low sacks, a strong outside game and two efficient targets in Bowers and Tucker. That supports roughly league-average-plus efficiency, in the 0.10-0.17 EPA-per-dropback range he has lived in during his good years. What won't hold is the touchdown rate. Red-zone success at 37% doesn't produce nine TDs on 26 throws over a full season, so expect closer to 1.7-2.0 a game. The deep efficiency on 17 attempts should also come down toward normal.

The risks are physical and structural. At 38, and coming off a 2025 accuracy slump, any regression in the intermediate game would show up first as turnovers. The run game is 29th in EPA, so defenses can tee off on the pass if the protection slips. An elite defense keeps the Raiders in close games, which has been his best game state (0.223 EPA within one score). That should keep the volume steady rather than spiky.
swingFactors: Intermediate accuracy and turnover rate at age 38

bets.reason: The Raiders are 4-0 against the spread with the league's 2nd-ranked defense, facing an offense 22nd in EPA. New England's secondary is missing Gonzalez and possibly Woods, which blunts its main defensive strength.
Nine of his 11 TDs came on 26 red-zone attempts with a 37% success rate, a pace well above his career norms. New England allows 1.5 passing TDs a game to quarterbacks.

bets.lean: At least one (in line with his 1.0 per game)
bets.reason: All four picks have come on intermediate throws, where he is 10.7 points under expected completion. He has thrown one in three of four games, and New England's pass defense ranks 5th in EPA.

confidence.note: Four games and small depth/red-zone samples, but the profile matches a long career baseline.
